2015_080_060215mtg.paragraph: Agenda and full board packet for the Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting of June 2, 2015, held at 7:00 p.m. at Athens High School, 4333 John R, Troy, Michigan 48085. Most of the packet is student recognition, running alphabetically from All-State winter athletes through the WordMasters Challenge. The business agenda awards the Administration and Services building roof replacement to J.D. Candler Roofing for $341,400.00 from the 2014 Capital Projects Fund, renews the Sodexo Management, Inc. food service contract, buys a food service point-of-sale system from Business Machine Company for $37,401.00, and raises paid lunch prices by $0.15.
2015_080_060215mtg.page:
**Meeting**
Regular meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education, Tuesday, June 2, 2015, 7:00 p.m., at Athens High School, 4333 John R, Troy, MI 48085. District offices: 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, 248.823.4000. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) and viewable at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Recognition (Item 2, A through HHH)**
Most of the agenda is end-of-year student recognition. Item A honors 2015 All-State winter athletes, chiefly synchronized swimmers coached by Lori Uchwal, plus swimmer Zachary Chen and basketball player John Van Hoef. Item B recognizes the 2014-15 synchronized swimming state champions; Item C lists Senior Scholar Athletes with a 3.5 grade point average. Item D recognizes a Troy Education Association donation to the Troy Foundation for Educational Excellence, presented by TEA President Tony Lucchi to Foundation representative Rich Maziasz for the Tony Spagnola Memorial Golf Classic on June 19th. Items E through HHH cover academic and arts competitions across Bemis, Leonard and Wattles elementary schools, Baker, Boulan Park, Larson and Smith middle schools, Athens and Troy high schools and International Academy East, read by Mike Jolly, Nancy Philippart, Karl Schmidt, Paula Fleming, Ida Edmunds and Todd Miletti.

**Personnel (Item 6)**
New hire Kerry Collins, .6 FTE Resource Room Teacher at Athens High School, on a probationary contract for the remainder of the 2014-2015 school year. Jordan Harris, formerly a UniServ Director with the Michigan Education Association, is recommended as Assistant Superintendent, Employee Services on a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure, effective August 3, 2015. Erica Rolack, most recently principal at Dixon Educational School in Detroit Public Schools, is recommended as Elementary Principal, effective July 1, 2015.

**Curriculum (Item 7)**
Adoption of the National Geographic Reach program (A, B, C levels) and the Grammar Gallery for ELD students in kindergarten through 5th grade, recommended May 5, 2015 by Elementary ELD Co-Chairpersons Christin Silagy and Danielle Andresen. Approval of a Michigan Council for Arts and Cultural Affairs grant to Troy High School that brought the Detroit Chamber Winds and Strings program to Troy High and Smith Middle School.

**Business (Item 8)**
A public hearing on the proposed 2015-2016 budget is set for June 23, 2015 at 7:00 p.m. at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois Road, Troy 48098, with notice published at least six days in advance. The Administration and Services building roof replacement is awarded to J.D. Candler Roofing at $341,400.00 from the 2014 Capital Projects Fund, under 2013 Bond Series 1 Bid Package #14. The Sodexo Management, Inc. food service contract is renewed for 2015/2016, with a guarantee amount of $152,159. A point-of-sale system is awarded to Business Machine Company at $37,401.00 from the 2014-2015 Food Services Fund. Paid lunch prices rise $0.15 under Section 205 of the Healthy, Hunger-Free Kids Act of 2010:

| Lunch price | 2014-15 student | 2014-15 adult | 2015-16 student | 2015-16 adult |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| K-5 | $2.25 | $3.25 | $2.40 | $3.40 |
| 6-12 | $2.50 | $3.25 | $2.65 | $3.40 |
| 6-12 | $3.50 | $3.50 | $3.65 | $3.65 |
| 6-12 | $3.75 | $4.75 | $3.90 | $4.90 |

**Other (Item 10)**
Ron Curtis of Barton Malow gives a 2013 Bond Program Series 1 construction update covering Troy High School classroom and storage additions, the Athens High School LGI renovation, and Boulan Park and Larson office additions. The Board also considers revising the rest of the 2015 meeting schedule so workshops fall on the first Tuesday and regular meetings on the third Tuesday, beginning September 2015.
2015_080_060215mtg.verbose:
**Meeting and format**
Board Meeting Agenda for the Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting of Tuesday, June 2, 2015 at 7:00 p.m. at Athens High School, 4333 John R, Troy, MI 48085 -- an off-site location noted on the district calendar as "June 2, 2015 (location: Athens)." District headquarters is 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, telephone 248.823.4000. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) and viewable at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Recognition -- Item 2, subitems A through HHH**
Item 2.A names the 2015 All-State winter athletes: synchronized swimmers Ellen Barker, Camille Bedford, Soumeeka Koneru, Kaylee Lee (2014 Colt of the Year), Julia Meng, Anjali Munasinghe, Daphne Samuel (2015 Colt of the Year), Hye-Kyung "Matilda" Seo (2015 Senior of the Year), Bhavya Sukhavasi, Amishi Taneja, Katie Ward and Christina Xu, all coached by Lori Uchwal; Zachary Chen (Senior, Troy High, boys swimming; All State 2015; school record for 200 Individual Medley; Coach Tom Buckheim); and John Van Hoef (Senior, Athens High, boys basketball; All State 2015 1st team; Academic All State; MVP Holiday Hoops Classic; Coach Dave Scott).
Item 2.B lists the 2014-15 Synchronized Swimming State Champions from Troy High and Athens High, including Monica Alluri, Priya Bandstra, Haya Beydoun, Michelle Cai, Inwoo Cho, June Choi, Joy Goldschmidt, Hanna Jung, Yejin Kim, Michelle Lebbos, Angela Li, Claire Li, Hemali Mistry, Anna Nichols, Jaclyn Anne Pabalan, Sabina Ravindran, Anisha Shukla, Sameeksha Venkatesh, Rohini Verma, Serena Yee and Kathleen Young, with Head Coach Lori Uchwal and assistants Katie Denning, Amanda Dine and Beth Borland. Item 2.C lists 2014-15 Senior Scholar Athletes carrying a 3.5 grade point average. Item 2.D recognizes the Troy Education Association for sponsoring a hole at the Tony Spagnola Memorial Golf Classic, the primary fundraiser for the Troy Foundation for Educational Excellence, held June 19th; TEA President Tony Lucchi presents the check to Foundation representative Rich Maziasz.
Items 2.E through 2.HHH honor competition results: an Athens student won Best in the State of Michigan/Best in Show at the DAFT Michigan Student Film Festival, in its 47th year, for "STEM Powered: Fostering Curiosity"; over 2,500 students competed at the State DECA Conference at the Amway Hotel in Grand Rapids; Destination Imagination Global Finals in May drew over 1,100 teams from 45 states, 7 Canadian provinces and 13 countries; an International Academy East Intel International Science and Engineering Fair entry (agenda-listed as Intel Science Talent Search) addressed "Self-Assembled Nanometer-sized Magnetic Sensors and Arrays for Bio-magnetic Imaging"; a Boulan Park student won the 19th Annual Jackie Robinson Art, Essay and Poetry Contest with a poem on "Courage"; Athens student Gloria took first in Michigan at the Japanese Speech Contest of March 28th at the Novi Civic Center, winning a $300 flight voucher; the Math Kangaroo Olympiad of March 19th drew 21,000 American students and over 6,000,000 worldwide; Larson Middle School reached "Emerald" status in Michigan Green Schools; nearly 22,000 students sat the National German Exam; the Baker Bobcats took 1st Place on May 1st in Road Scholar, Bottle Rocket and Picture This and finished 4th place among the top 48 qualifying Science Olympiad teams in Michigan, while Boulan Park fields 30 students across 23 events; Troy High's Symphonic Orchestra won the highest award at the National Festival in Florida; and in the USA Biology Olympiad 7,766 students took the exam nationwide, 12 Troy High semifinalists placed in the top 10%, and one reached finalist level (top 20 in the U.S.) and placed 6th in the National Biology Competition against over 4,000 students. Further items cover the Arctic Bookmark Contest, the American Mathematics Competitions (more than 350,000 students), Business Professionals of America, the Chemistry Olympiad, FIRST Robotics, HOSA, MATHCOUNTS, Math Madness, the Michigan Youth Arts Festival, MIT INSPIRE, the MSBOA All-State Band, the National French, Japanese, Spanish and Language Arts exams, Purple Comet, Robofest, the Siemens Competition and the WordMasters Challenge.

**Personnel -- Item 6**
6.A recommends a probationary contract for the remainder of the 2014-2015 school year for Kerry Collins, .6 FTE Resource Room Teacher at Athens High School. Her sketch lists a B.A. from the University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, May 2009 (major History, minor Psychology); an M.A. from Oakland University, Detroit, April 2012 (Special Education); a Michigan Professional Certificate in January 2015; Resource Room Teacher in the Waterford School District January 2013 to April 2015; Social Studies Teacher at Chandler Park Academy, Harper Woods, August 2010 to January 2013; and Guest Teacher in the Troy School District August 2009 to August 2010. Resident community: Shelby Township, Michigan.
6.B recommends Mr. Jordan Harris as Assistant Superintendent, Employee Services. He comes from the Michigan Education Association, where he spent the past 6 years as UniServ Director, first for Lansing Community College and then for Wayne County, and earlier spent 4 years as an attorney with Collins & Blaha, P.C. in Farmington Hills. He received his Juris Doctor in 2004 from the Michigan State University College of Law and his Master of Science in Labor Relations and Human Resources and Bachelor of Arts in International Relations from Michigan State University in 2003 and 2001. The resolution issues a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure, with duties beginning August 3, 2015.
6.C recommends Ms. Erica Rolack as Elementary Principal (the agenda lists the position as Principal, Leonard Elementary School). She comes from Detroit Public Schools after 16 years there -- 6 years as a middle school teacher, 5 as an elementary teacher, one as an instructional specialist, 3 as an assistant principal and the past year as principal at Dixon Educational School. She earned a Bachelor's in Elementary Education from Wayne State University in 1999 and a Master's in Educational Psychology in 2007, and would begin July 1, 2015.

**Curriculum -- Item 7**
7.A adopts the elementary ELD materials recommended at the May 5, 2015 Board meeting by Elementary ELD Co-Chairpersons Christin Silagy and Danielle Andresen: the National Geographic Reach program (A, B, C levels) and the Grammar Gallery for ELD students in kindergarten through 5th grade, for 2015-2016. 7.B approves a Michigan Council for Arts and Cultural Affairs grant to Troy High School for a project that brought the Detroit Chamber Winds and Strings program to Troy High School and Smith Middle School through lectures, demonstrations and a shared concert.

**Business -- Item 8**
8.A sets a public hearing on the proposed 2015-2016 budget for June 23, 2015 at a regular Board meeting beginning at 7:00 p.m. at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois Road, Troy 48098. Michigan law requires notice at least six (6) days beforehand, including in 11-point bold faced type the statement that the property tax millage rate proposed to be levied to support the proposed budget will be a subject of the hearing. Exhibit A, signed by Board Secretary Paula Fleming, states copies will be available at the Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, from 8:00 a.m. until 5:00 p.m., Wednesday, June 17, 2015 through Tuesday, June 23, 2015.
8.B awards the Administration and Services buildings roof replacement to J.D. Candler Roofing in the amount of $341,400.00, approved as an expenditure of the 2014 Capital Projects Fund. Bids were reviewed by Mr. Rob Carson, Director of Maintenance and Operations, Mr. Ron Curtis of Barton Malow, and Ms. Michelle Kerns, Owners Representative. A Letter of Intent/Notice to Proceed dated May 20, 2015 from Douglas Madden, Sr. Project Manager, Barton Malow Company, is addressed to JD Candler, 31111 Industrial Drive, Livonia, MI 48150, under "2013 Bond Series 1 Bid Package #14, Administration & Services Building Roofing Replacement," directing shop drawings to Barton Malow Co and TMP Associates, with that cost reimbursed if the project were canceled on or before the award date of June 2nd, 2015. Contact: Doug Madden at (248) 219.4295; Central File: 104077.
8.C renews the food services contract with Sodexo Management, Inc. for the 2015/2016 school year; the Board approved the original contract resolution on May 6, 2014, and renewal requires annual approval by both the Michigan Department of Education and the Troy Board of Education. Ruby Zavala, Departmental Analyst, Food Service Contracts, Child Nutrition Programs, MDE, PO Box 30008, Lansing MI 48909, emailed approval of the FSMC renewal on Tuesday, May 26, 2015 at 8:19 AM, copying Katherine Fuller; Rick West forwarded it at 9:57:10 AM to Patricia R Orczykowski, copying Gayle M Moran. West's May 6, 2015 letter to Cheryl Schubel of MDE lists the RFP adjustments: a Meal Equivalent Factor for 2015-2016 of $3.2300; an administration fee rising from $0.13 in 2014-15 to $0.1339 in 2015-16, an increase of 3.0%; a management fee rising from $0.119 to $0.1225, an increase of 3.0%; a guarantee amount for 2015-2016 of $152,159, subject to adjustment for legislation such as the Healthy, Hunger-Free Kids Act of 2010; and no capital equipment planned for FSMC purchase in 2015/16.
8.D awards the Point of Sale System contract to Business Machine Company in the amount of $37,401.00 as an expenditure of the 2014-2015 Food Services Fund. Bids were reviewed by Kris Young, Director of Technology; Gayle Moran, General Manager, Sodexo Food Services; and John Foster, Convergent Technology Partners. Moran's May 6, 2015 memo on BID 9809 -- Food Service POS Equipment states the specification was to furnish and deliver 39 Point of Sale units for the School Lunch Program and that invitations to bid went to seven potential bidders. The 5/28/2015 bid tabulation reads:

| Vendor | Amount |
| --- | --- |
| Business Machines Company | $37,401.00 |
| Crimson Solutions, LLC | $37,245.00 (alternate bid of $29,250, not to spec) |
| Food Service Solutions, Inc. | $35,061.00 |
| Heartland Payment Solutions, Inc. | $58,890.00 |
| Scan Technology, Inc. | $46,761.00 (alternate bid of $35,841, not to spec) |
| TekVisions, Inc. | $34,203.00 |

8.E adopts a paid lunch price adjustment required by Section 205 of the Healthy, Hunger-Free Kids Act of 2010, using the paid lunch equity (PLE) tool from the USDA Food and Nutrition Service. Rick West's May 21, 2015 memo to Superintendent Dr. Rich Machesky states that Troy's calculation yields a weighted average price of $2.55 against a 2015-16 weighted average requirement of $2.70, so a $0.15 increase per paid lunch is recommended:

| Lunch price | 2014-15 student | 2014-15 adult | 2015-16 student | 2015-16 adult |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| K-5 | $2.25 | $3.25 | $2.40 | $3.40 |
| 6-12 | $2.50 | $3.25 | $2.65 | $3.40 |
| 6-12 | $3.50 | $3.50 | $3.65 | $3.65 |
| 6-12 | $3.75 | $4.75 | $3.90 | $4.90 |

The attached PLE worksheets show a SY 2015-16 weighted average price requirement of $2.70 (also $2.70 rounded down to the nearest 5 cents), a SY 2014-15 unrounded price requirement of $2.62, and a note that prices are based on adjusting the SY 2014-2015 requirement by the 2% rate increase plus the Consumer Price Index (2.19%). The October 2014 price calculator lists 34,481 paid lunches at $2.25 generating $77,582.25; 16,134 at $2.50 generating $40,335.00; 9,942 at $3.50 generating $34,797.00; and 1,169 at $3.75 generating $4,383.75, totaling 61,726 lunches and $157,098.00 of monthly revenue at a weighted average price of $2.55. The optional estimation block uses the same counts at $2.50, $2.75, $3.75 and $4.00 to produce $86,202.50, $44,368.50, $37,282.50 and $4,676.00, a total of $172,529.50 and a weighted average price of $2.80. The sheet records a total price increase for SY 2015-16 of $0.15, a remaining increase carried forward to SY 2016-17 of $0.05, and figures of $2.65 and a 10 cent cap on the required price increase line.

**Other -- Item 10**
10.A is a report requiring no action by Ron Curtis, Senior Project Manager from Barton Malow, on the 2013 Bond Program Series 1 construction update dated 6.2.15, prepared by Barton Malow | TMP. Troy High School classroom and storage additions and the Boulan Park and Larson office additions carry completion dates of approximately December 2015; Troy Athens High School's LGI and multi-use classroom renovation is listed for Spring 2015. Planned 2015 projects: BP #8, Athens High School mechanical and electrical upgrades, out for bids August 2015; BP #9, Larson and Boulan Park mechanical and electrical upgrades and site paving, contracts awarded; BP #14, Administration & Service Center roofing, bids received May 13, 2015; BP #15, Costello and Wass elementary roofing; BP #16, Hamilton Elementary doors, flooring and mechanical and electrical upgrades; and BP #17, International Academy East, converting the pool to an LGI room and replacing doors and windows -- the last three out for bids December 2015.
10.B asks the Board to revise its meeting schedule for the remainder of the 2015 calendar year so that workshops fall on the first Tuesday of each month followed by regular Board meetings on the third Tuesday, beginning in September 2015. The attached calendar, dated 01.13.15, shows regular meetings at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, at 7:00 p.m. on January 13 (Organizational & Regular Meeting), February 3, March 3, April 14, May 5, June 2 (location: Athens), June 16, July 7 and August 4, 2015, with the fall dates overstruck and revised to September 15, October 20, November 17 and December 15, 2015 and January 19, 2016. Workshops at the Administrative Center, 4400 Livernois, at 6:00 p.m. run January 20, a Winter Retreat Saturday, January 24 at 9:30 a.m., February 10, March 17, April 21, May 19 and June 9, 2015, with fall workshops revised to September 1, October 6, November 10 and December 1, 2015.
